<blockquote>Although direct research on this topic is difficult, it seems clear that malevolent stockbrokers such as Bernie Madoff do not qualify as psychopaths: They are corporate Machiavellians who use deliberate, strategic procedures for exploiting others. A genuine psychopath, even at the subclinical level, lacks the self-control to orchestrate the schemes of a shrewd stockbroker.<ref name="Paulhus-2014">{{cite journal |last1=Paulhus |first1=Delroy L. |title=Toward a Taxonomy of Dark Personalities |journal=Current Directions in Psychological Science |date=December 2014 |volume=23 |issue=6 |pages=421–426 |doi=10.1177/0963721414547737 }}</ref></blockquote>

In a research paper, Daniel Jones and others stated that a person high on Machiavellianism would also be possibly drawn to cybercrime, noting that "although we did not directly assess crimes, we did find patterns of system infiltration that were different among the three traits, with Machiavellianism being associated with the stealthiest approach among the three traits." They also stated that Machiavellianism would only be associated with crime if the "benefits outweighed the risks". They went on to clarify that this is opposed to individuals high in psychopathy, whom are prone to crime regardless of the situation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Padilla |first2=Edgar |last3=Curtis |first3=Shelby R. |last4=Kiekintveld |first4=Christopher |title=Network discovery and scanning strategies and the Dark Triad |journal=Computers in Human Behavior |date=September 2021 |volume=122 |article-number=106799 |doi=10.1016/j.chb.2021.106799 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hare |first1=Robert D. |title=Psychopathy: A Clinical Construct Whose Time Has Come |journal=Criminal Justice and Behavior |date=March 1996 |volume=23 |issue=1 |pages=25–54 |doi=10.1177/0093854896023001004}}</ref>

===Other "dark" groupings===
Machiavellianism has been featured in many other groupings of dark traits, such as the dark tetrad, which adds [[everyday sadism|sadism]] to the dark triad traits.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Međedović |first1=Janko |last2=Petrović |first2=Boban |title=The Dark Tetrad: Structural Properties and Location in the Personality Space |journal=Journal of Individual Differences |date=November 2015 |volume=36 |issue=4 |pages=228–236 |doi=10.1027/1614-0001/a000179 }}</ref> The characteristics of Machiavellianism have also been viewed as potentially correlated with sadism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bonfá-Araujo |first1=Bruno |last2=Lima-Costa |first2=Ariela Raissa |last3=Hauck-Filho |first3=Nelson |last4=Jonason |first4=Peter Karl |title=Considering sadism in the shadow of the Dark Triad traits: A meta-analytic review of the Dark Tetrad |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=October 2022 |volume=197 |article-number=111767 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2022.111767 |quote=Finally, sadism is potentially more similar to psychopathy and Machiavellianism, than narcissism. }}</ref>

The paper titled "The Dark Core of Personality" introduced a theoretical framework to understand various "dark traits" in personality as manifestations of a single underlying factor called the ''Dark Factor of Personality''. This factor represents a general dispositional tendency where individuals prioritize their own utility (self-interest) at the expense of others, often justifying their actions through certain beliefs. The concept of D encapsulates all of the main "dark traits", with the addition of Spitefulness, Egoism, [[Moral disengagement|Moral Disengagement]], Entitlement, and Self-interest.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Moshagen |first1=Morten |last2=Zettler |first2=Ingo |last3=Hilbig |first3=Benjamin E. |title=Measuring the dark core of personality |journal=Psychological Assessment |date=February 2020 |volume=32 |issue=2 |pages=182–196 |id={{ProQuest|2318137173}} |doi=10.1037/pas0000778 |pmid=31613123 }}</ref> The authors of the study argued that while Machiavellianism, along with other dark traits like Narcissism and Psychopathy, has its unique features, it also shares a common core with these traits, which is encapsulated in the D factor. This means that people who score high in Machiavellianism tend to exhibit behaviors that prioritize their own benefit over others' which correlate with characteristics that align with the D factor.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Moshagen |first1=Morten |last2=Hilbig |first2=Benjamin E. |last3=Zettler |first3=Ingo |title=The dark core of personality |journal=Psychological Review |date=October 2018 |volume=125 |issue=5 |pages=656–688 |doi=10.1037/rev0000111 |pmid=29999338 |url=https://curis.ku.dk/portal/da/publications/the-dark-core-of-personality(3c800140-5419-4258-a7ce-ecbe20236e5b).html |url-access=subscription }}</ref> It is said that manipulativeness and callousness is responsible for the covariances among the dark personalities in general.<ref name="Jones Figueredo Core of Darkness"/>

The [[light triad]] is a personality model that contrasts the dark triad, which comprises Kantianism, faith in humanity, and humanism. Kantianism was compared to Machiavellianism as its opposite, as it is characterized by a non-exploitative orientation. Both Kantianism and Machiavellianism are traits which are tongue-in-cheek references to philosophers. The "Light Triad" and its characteristics were most strongly negatively correlated with Machiavellianism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kaufman |first1=Scott Barry |last2=Yaden |first2=David Bryce |last3=Hyde |first3=Elizabeth |last4=Tsukayama |first4=Eli |title=The Light vs. Dark Triad of Personality: Contrasting Two Very Different Profiles of Human Nature |journal=Frontiers in Psychology |date=12 March 2019 |volume=10 |article-number=467 |doi=10.3389/fpsyg.2019.00467 |doi-access=free |pmid=30914993 |pmc=6423069 }}</ref>

==DSM: Trait, not disorder==

Machiavellianism has never been considered a disorder, nor has it been referenced in any version of the ''[[Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders]]'' or [[International Classification of Diseases]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.psychiatry.org/psychiatrists/practice/dsm/about-dsm/history-of-the-dsm |title=Psychiatry.org - DSM History}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=https://www.britannica.com/science/Machiavellianism |title=Machiavellianism &#124; Definition, Politics, Psychology, & Facts &#124; Britannica |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia Britannica }}</ref> It has always been treated solely as a personality construct. It is primarily studied by personality psychologists, as it is a non-clinical personality style.{{sfn|McHoskey|Worzel|Szyarto|1998}}<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1093/oxfordhb/9780192897114.013.12 |quote=Machiavellianism is the only one of the D3 that does not have its origin in clinical psychology. |chapter=Explorations of the Shadow Realm |title=The Oxford Handbook of Individual Differences in Organizational Contexts |date=2024 |last1=Harms |first1=Peter D. |last2=Landay |first2=Karen |last3=Fezzey |first3=Tyler |pages=122–139 |isbn=978-0-19-289711-4 }}</ref>

==Relations with other personality traits==

There is immense literature concerning the relationships between Machiavellianism and other personality dimensions, such as the traits in the [[Big Five personality traits|Big Five trait model]].<ref name="Lee-2005"/> Machiavellianism has also been related to interpersonal aggression and hostile behavior.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Neria |first2=Adon L. |title=The Dark Triad and dispositional aggression |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=November 2015 |volume=86 |pages=360–364 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2015.06.021}}</ref>

===Big Five===

Mach-IV scores are negatively correlated with [[agreeableness]] (''r'' = −0.47) and [[conscientiousness]] (''r'' = −0.34), two dimensions of the Big Five personality model (NEO-PI-R).<ref name="Paulhus-2002"/> The FFMI corrects for this by including aspects of high conscientiousness in the scale (e.g. order, deliberation).<ref name="Collison-2018"/> Additionally, Machiavellianism correlates more highly with the [[honesty-humility]] dimension of the six-factor [[HEXACO model]] than with any of the big five dimensions.<ref name="Jones-2009">{{cite book |title=Handbook of Individual Differences in Social Behavior |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookindividu00lear |url-access=limited |year=2009 |publisher=The Guilford Press |location=New York/London |isbn=978-1-59385-647-2 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/handbookindividu00lear/page/n274 257]–273 |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Paulhus |first2=Delroy L. |editor=Leary, Mark R. |editor2=Hoyle, Rick H |chapter=Chapter 7. Machiavellianism}}</ref> Machiavellianism has also been located within the [[interpersonal circumplex]], which consists of the two independent dimensions of agency and communion.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rauthmann |first1=John F. |last2=Kolar |first2=Gerald P. |title=Positioning the Dark Triad in the interpersonal circumplex: The friendly-dominant narcissist, hostile-submissive Machiavellian, and hostile-dominant psychopath? |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=April 2013 |volume=54 |issue=5 |pages=622–627 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2012.11.021}}</ref><ref name="McHoskey-1995"/><ref name="Jones-2010">{{cite book |doi=10.1002/9781118001868.ch15 |chapter=Differentiating the Dark Triad within the Interpersonal Circumplex |title=Handbook of Interpersonal Psychology |date=2010 |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Paulhus |first2=Delroy L. |pages=249–267 |isbn=978-0-470-47160-9}}</ref> Agency refers to the motivation to succeed and to individuate the self, whereas communion refers to the motivation to merge with others and to support group interests.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gurtman |first1=Michael B. |title=Exploring Personality with the Interpersonal Circumplex |journal=Social and Personality Psychology Compass |date=July 2009 |volume=3 |issue=4 |pages=601–619 |doi=10.1111/j.1751-9004.2009.00172.x}}</ref> Machiavellianism lies in the quadrant of the circumplex defined by high agency and low communion.<ref name="Jones-2009"/> Machiavellianism has been found to lie diagonally opposite from a circumplex construct called ''self-construal'', a tendency to prefer communion over agency. This suggests that people high in Machiavellianism do not simply wish to achieve, they wish to do so at the expense of (or at least without regard to) others.<ref name="Jones-2009"/><ref name="Jones-2010"/>

=== Hot and cold empathy ===
There are two distinct types of [[empathy]] which people use to relate to each other which are referred to as hot and cold empathy.{{sfn|Lyons|2019|p=16}}<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Arefi |first1=Mozhgan |title=Present of a causal model for social function based on theory of mind with mediating of Machiavellian beliefs and hot empathy |journal=Procedia - Social and Behavioral Sciences |date=2010 |volume=5 |pages=694–697 |doi=10.1016/j.sbspro.2010.07.167 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
Cold empathy (or ''cognitive'' empathy) refers to the understanding of how others might react to one's actions or a certain event.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ang |first1=Rebecca P. |last2=Goh |first2=Dion H. |title=Cyberbullying Among Adolescents: The Role of Affective and Cognitive Empathy, and Gender |journal=Child Psychiatry & Human Development |date=August 2010 |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=387–397 |doi=10.1007/s10578-010-0176-3 |pmid=20238160}}</ref>
Hot empathy (or ''emotional/affective'' empathy) refers to the emotional reaction others might have to the emotions of another person.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cox |first1=Christine L. |last2=Uddin |first2=Lucina Q. |last3=Di Martino |first3=Adriana |last4=Castellanos |first4=F. Xavier |last5=Milham |first5=Michael P. |last6=Kelly |first6=Clare |title=The balance between feeling and knowing: affective and cognitive empathy are reflected in the brain's intrinsic functional dynamics |journal=Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience |date=August 2012 |volume=7 |issue=6 |pages=727–737 |doi=10.1093/scan/nsr051 |pmid=21896497 |pmc=3427869}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |pmc=8989800 |date=2021 |last1=Thompson |first1=N. M. |last2=Van Reekum |first2=C. M. |last3=Chakrabarti |first3=B. |title=Cognitive and Affective Empathy Relate Differentially to Emotion Regulation |journal=Affective Science |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=118–134 |doi=10.1007/s42761-021-00062-w |pmid=35465047}}</ref>
Machiavellianism was consistently negatively correlated with affective empathy in practically every study.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pajevic |first1=Marija |last2=Vukosavljevic-Gvozden |first2=Tatjana |last3=Stevanovic |first3=Nikola |last4=Neumann |first4=Craig S. |title=The relationship between the Dark Tetrad and a two-dimensional view of empathy |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=March 2018 |volume=123 |pages=125–130 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2017.11.009 }}</ref><ref name="Massey-Abernathy-2016"/>{{sfn|Lyons|2019|pp=17–18}}<ref name="Blotner-2021">{{cite journal |last1=Blötner |first1=Christian |last2=Steinmayr |first2=Ricarda |last3=Bergold |first3=Sebastian |title=Malicious mind readers? A meta-analysis on Machiavellianism and cognitive and affective empathy |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=October 2021 |volume=181 |article-number=111023 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2021.111023}}</ref> Machiavellianism was also negatively correlated with affective resonance (feeling good when others feel good) and positively associated with affective dissonance (e.g. feeling happy when others are sad).<ref name="Blotner-2021"/> People high in Machiavellianism tend to have a better understanding of cold empathy and do not feel hot empathy which explains why they seem cold and uncaring.<ref name="Taylor">{{Cite magazine |last=Taylor |first=Ben |title=Machiavellianism, Cognition, and Emotion: Understanding how the Machiavellian Thinks, Feels, and Thrives |url=https://psychcentral.com/lib/machiavellianism-cognition-and-emotion-understanding-how-the-machiavellian-thinks-feels-and-thrives/ |magazine=Psych Central |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330021043/https://psychcentral.com/lib/machiavellianism-cognition-and-emotion-understanding-how-the-machiavellian-thinks-feels-and-thrives/ |archive-date=2019-03-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Paal |first1=Tunde |last2=Bereczkei |first2=Tamas |title=Adult theory of mind, cooperation, Machiavellianism: The effect of mindreading on social relations |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=August 2007 |volume=43 |issue=3 |pages=541–551 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2006.12.021|url=https://durham-repository.worktribe.com/output/1202739 }}</ref> Research results have also suggested that High Machs are deficient only at the level of affective empathy (sharing of emotions), whereas their cognitive empathy is intact, even high.<ref name="Al Ain-2013">{{cite journal |last1=Al Aïn |first1=Syrina |last2=Carré |first2=Arnaud |last3=Fantini-Hauwel |first3=Carole |last4=Baudouin |first4=Jean-Yves |last5=Besche-Richard |first5=Chrystel |title=What is the emotional core of the multidimensional Machiavellian personality trait? |journal=Frontiers in Psychology |date=2013 |volume=4 |page=454 |doi=10.3389/fpsyg.2013.00454 |doi-access=free |pmid=23885245 |pmc=3717508}}</ref><ref>
* {{cite journal |last1=Barnett |first1=Mark A. |last2=Thompson |first2=Shannon |title=The Role of Perspective Taking and Empathy in Children's Machiavellianism, Prosocial Behavior, and Motive for Helping |journal=The Journal of Genetic Psychology |date=September 1985 |volume=146 |issue=3 |pages=295–305 |doi=10.1080/00221325.1985.9914459}}
* {{cite book |last1=Repacholi |first1=Betty |last2=Slaughter |first2=Virginia |last3=Pritchard |first3=Michelle |last4=Gibbs |first4=Vicki |chapter=Theory of mind, Machiavellism, and social functioning in childhood |pages=99–120 |editor-last1=Repacholi |editor-last2=Slaughter |editor-first1=Betty |editor-first2=Virginia |title=Individual Differences in Theory of Mind |date=2004 |isbn=978-1-135-43234-8 |doi=10.4324/9780203488508}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Richell |first1=R.A |last2=Mitchell |first2=D.G.V |last3=Newman |first3=C |last4=Leonard |first4=A |last5=Baron-Cohen |first5=S |last6=Blair |first6=R.J.R |title=Theory of mind and psychopathy: can psychopathic individuals read the 'language of the eyes'? |journal=Neuropsychologia |date=2003 |volume=41 |issue=5 |pages=523–526 |doi=10.1016/S0028-3932(02)00175-6 |pmid=12559146}}</ref> Another study suggested that high Machs are deficient at both kinds  of empathy.<ref name="Lyons-2010">{{cite journal |last1=Lyons |first1=M. |last2=Caldwell |first2=T. |last3=Shultz |first3=S. |title=Mind-reading and manipulation — Is Machiavellianism related to theory of mind? |journal=Journal of Evolutionary Psychology |date=September 2010 |volume=8 |issue=3 |pages=261–274 |doi=10.1556/JEP.8.2010.3.7}}</ref> Studies also assert that high Machs do not feel guilt or remorse over the consequences of their manipulations.<ref>See the following:

* {{cite book |doi=10.1037/14854-005 |chapter=The nature of Machiavellianism: Distinct patterns of misbehavior |title=The dark side of personality: Science and practice in social, personality, and clinical psychology |date=2016 |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |pages=87–107 |isbn=978-1-4338-2187-5 }}
* {{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Slomski |first2=Sarah |last3=Partyka |first3=Jamie |title=The Dark Triad at work: How toxic employees get their way |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=February 2012 |volume=52 |issue=3 |pages=449–453 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2011.11.008 }}
* {{cite journal |last1=Lee |first1=Kibeom |last2=Ashton |first2=Michael C. |title=Psychopathy, Machiavellianism, and Narcissism in the Five-Factor Model and the HEXACO model of personality structure |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=May 2005 |volume=38 |issue=7 |pages=1571–1582 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2004.09.016 }}
* {{cite journal |last1=Murphy |first1=Pamela R. |title=Attitude, Machiavellianism and the rationalization of misreporting |journal=Accounting, Organizations and Society |date=May 2012 |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=242–259 |doi=10.1016/j.aos.2012.04.002 }}
* {{cite journal |last1=McHoskey |first1=John W. |last2=Worzel |first2=William |last3=Szyarto |first3=Christopher |title=Machiavellianism and psychopathy |journal=Journal of Personality and Social Psychology |date=1998 |volume=74 |issue=1 |pages=192–210 |doi=10.1037/0022-3514.74.1.192 |pmid=9457782 }}
</ref>{{sfn|Leary|Hoyle|2013|p=93}} High Machs are less likely to be altruistic, and they are less likely to be concerned with the problems of others.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/beautiful-minds/the-light-triad-vs-dark-triad-of-personality/ |title=The Light Triad vs. Dark Triad of Personality |first=Scott Barry |last=Kaufman |website=Scientific American Blog Network}}</ref> High Machs are also less emotionally expressive and have a hard time recognizing and understanding the emotional states of others.{{sfn|McHoskey|Worzel|Szyarto|1998}} One study proposed that High Machs have more automatic (that is, unconscious) recognition of other's negative emotions more than low Machs, and though they don't internalize these feelings, the understanding of those emotions may in fact aid in the manipulation of others.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bagozzi |first1=Richard P. |last2=Verbeke |first2=Willem J. M. I. |last3=Dietvorst |first3=Roeland C. |last4=Belschak |first4=Frank D. |last5=van den Berg |first5=Wouter E. |last6=Rietdijk |first6=Wim J. R. |title=Theory of Mind and Empathic Explanations of Machiavellianism: A Neuroscience Perspective |journal=Journal of Management |date=November 2013 |volume=39 |issue=7 |pages=1760–1798 |doi=10.1177/0149206312471393}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Massey-Abernathy |first1=Amber |last2=Byrd-Craven |first2=Jennifer |title=Seeing but Not Feeling: Machiavellian Traits in Relation to Physiological Empathetic Responding and Life Experiences |journal=Adaptive Human Behavior and Physiology |date=September 2016 |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=252–266 |doi=10.1007/s40750-016-0041-0 |quote=However, some individuals high on Machiavellian traits have been shown to be skilled at affective-perspective taking and thereby may appear to exhibit an empathic response }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1037/14854-005 |chapter=The nature of Machiavellianism: Distinct patterns of misbehavior |title=The dark side of personality: Science and practice in social, personality, and clinical psychology |date=2016 |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |pages=87–107 |isbn=978-1-4338-2187-5 |quote=Following these conflicting findings, neurological research by Bagozzi and colleagues (2013) discovered that Machiavellian individuals are more attuned to others with respect to the detection of negative emotions but less likely to take another's perspective. This negative association suggests an ability trade-off in Machiavellianism. }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Waldman |first1=David A. |last2=Ward |first2=M.K. |last3=Becker |first3=William J. |title=Neuroscience in Organizational Behavior |journal=Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior |date=21 March 2017 |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=425–444 |doi=10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-032516-113316 }}</ref> Children who scored higher on Machiavellianism showed a lack of empathy and more delinquent behaviors compared to those who scored lower, such as a lack of guilt, lying, cheating, and truancy.<ref name="Loftus">{{cite journal |last1=Loftus |first1=Shay T. |last2=Glenwick |first2=David S. |title=Machiavellianism and Empathy in an Adolescent Residential Psychiatric Population |journal=Residential Treatment for Children & Youth |date=December 2001 |volume=19 |issue=2 |pages=39–57 |doi=10.1300/J007v19n02_04 }}</ref> A 2025 study concluded that "by and large, Machiavellianism was more strongly negatively related to affective empathy".<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Blötner | first1=Christian | last2=Kaminski | first2=Alexander | title=Challenging the "Empathic Deficits Hypothesis" of Machiavellianism | journal=Journal of Individual Differences | date=2025 | volume=46 | issue=2 | pages=97–108 | doi=10.1027/1614-0001/a000440 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

Some authors have stated that since Machiavellianism is so diametrically opposed to empathy, it should be included in empathy scales as the polar opposite. Total scores on Machiavellianism and empathy were "significantly negatively correlated".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Andrew |first1=J. |last2=Cooke |first2=M. |last3=Muncer |first3=S.J. |title=The relationship between empathy and Machiavellianism: An alternative to empathizing–systemizing theory |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=April 2008 |volume=44 |issue=5 |pages=1203–1211 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2007.11.014 }}</ref>

=== Unemotionality ===
One of the primary traits of machiavellianism is a detached, unemotional attitude and lack of affect in regards to others.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heym |first1=Nadja |last2=Firth |first2=Jennifer |last3=Kibowski |first3=Fraenze |last4=Sumich |first4=Alexander |last5=Egan |first5=Vincent |last6=Bloxsom |first6=Claire A. J. |title=Empathy at the Heart of Darkness: Empathy Deficits That Bind the Dark Triad and Those That Mediate Indirect Relational Aggression |journal=Frontiers in Psychiatry |date=12 March 2019 |volume=10 |article-number=95 |doi=10.3389/fpsyt.2019.00095 |doi-access=free |pmid=30930800 |pmc=6423894}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Machiavellianism {{!}} Definition, Politics, Psychology, & Facts {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/science/Machiavellianism |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref> Christie and Geis noted that the primary difference between high machs and low machs was the degree of emotion invested in interpersonal relations, with those scoring high having the lowest.<ref name="Wastell-2003">{{cite journal |last1=Wastell |first1=Colin |last2=Booth |first2=Alexandra |title=Machiavellianism: An Alexithymic Perspective |journal=Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology |date=December 2003 |volume=22 |issue=6 |pages=730–744 |doi=10.1521/jscp.22.6.730.22931}}</ref>{{sfn|Christie|Geis|1970|p=312}}
Research has been done on the extent of the low emotionality of those who score high on the Machiavellianism scale.<ref name="Jonason1">{{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Krause |first2=Laura |title=The emotional deficits associated with the Dark Triad traits: Cognitive empathy, affective empathy, and alexithymia |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=September 2013 |volume=55 |issue=5 |pages=532–537 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2013.04.027}}</ref> Doris Mcllwain noted that "Machiavellians do not inhabit the realm of emotion in the same way as others, yet they use it to manipulate others. They do not experience feelings, empathy, or morality in normative ways. yet they are consummate manipulators and deceivers precisely by playing upon these sentiments and convictions in others. Thus they induce in others the guilt they hardly feel themselves."<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1037/12352-012 |chapter=Young Machiavellians and the traces of shame: Coping with vulnerability to a toxic affect |title=Narcissism and Machiavellianism in youth: Implications for the development of adaptive and maladaptive behavior |date=2011 |last1=McIlwain |first1=Doris |pages=213–231 |publisher=American Psychological Association |location=Washington |isbn=978-1-4338-0845-6}}</ref> A study done by Farah Ali and others noted that Machiavellianism seems to have emotional reactions to stimuli similar to primary psychopathy, differing only in higher levels of anxiety, which those who score highly on machiavellianism may be prone to.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ali |first1=Farah |last2=Amorim |first2=Ines Sousa |last3=Chamorro-Premuzic |first3=Tomas |title=Empathy deficits and trait emotional intelligence in psychopathy and Machiavellianism |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=November 2009 |volume=47 |issue=7 |pages=758–762 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2009.06.016}}</ref>{{sfn|McHoskey|Worzel|Szyarto|1998}} Machiavellianism has an unclear relation with anxiety levels, some researchers have found positive correlations, while some have found no relation at all.<ref name="Czibor-2017">{{cite journal |last1=Czibor |first1=Andrea |last2=Szabo |first2=Zsolt Peter |last3=Jones |first3=Daniel N. |last4=Zsido |first4=Andras Norbert |last5=Paal |first5=Tunde |last6=Szijjarto |first6=Linda |last7=Carre |first7=Jessica R. |last8=Bereczkei |first8=Tamas |title=Male and female face of Machiavellianism: Opportunism or anxiety? |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=October 2017 |volume=117 |pages=221–229 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2017.06.002|url=https://durham-repository.worktribe.com/output/1201046 }}</ref> High Machs demonstrate reduced skills in expressing their emotions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pilch |first1=Irena |title=Machiavellianism, emotional intelligence and social competence: Are Machiavellians interpersonally skilled? |journal=Polish Psychological Bulletin |date=2008 |volume=39 |issue=3 |id={{CORE output|210570121}} {{ProQuest|1323960306}} |doi=10.2478/v10059-008-0017-4 |hdl=20.500.12128/9317 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szijjarto |first1=Linda |last2=Bereczkei |first2=Tamas |title=The Machiavellians' 'Cool Syndrome': They Experience Intensive Feelings but Have Difficulties in Expressing Their Emotions |journal=Current Psychology |date=June 2015 |volume=34 |issue=2 |pages=363–375 |doi=10.1007/s12144-014-9262-1}}</ref>

A 2014 analysis discovered that, in addition to acting for mostly self interest and profit, High Machs used significantly less words when referring to emotional involvement. They concluded that "this study confirmed previous findings that High Machs have a cool and rational character and a pro-self orientation and showed that their lack of group orientation may account for their low cooperation in social dilemmas."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Czibor |first1=Andrea |last2=Vincze |first2=Orsolya |last3=Bereczkei |first3=Tamas |title=Feelings and motives underlying Machiavellian behavioural strategies; narrative reports in a social dilemma situation |journal=International Journal of Psychology |date=December 2014 |volume=49 |issue=6 |pages=519–524 |doi=10.1002/ijop.12077 |pmid=24842298}}</ref>

[[Alexithymia]] is also considered a key trait that has correlations with Machiavellianism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wastell |first1=Colin |last2=Booth |first2=Alexandra |title=Machiavellianism: An Alexithymic Perspective |journal=Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology |date=December 2003 |volume=22 |issue=6 |pages=730–744 |doi=10.1521/jscp.22.6.730.22931 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Al Aïn |first1=Syrina |last2=Carré |first2=Arnaud |last3=Fantini-Hauwel |first3=Carole |last4=Baudouin |first4=Jean-Yves |last5=Besche-Richard |first5=Chrystel |title=What is the emotional core of the multidimensional Machiavellian personality trait? |journal=Frontiers in Psychology |date=2013 |volume=4 |page=454 |doi=10.3389/fpsyg.2013.00454 |doi-access=free |pmid=23885245 |pmc=3717508 }}</ref> It is the lack of awareness of one's own emotions as well as the emotions of others.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Leonard |first1=Jayne |title=Alexithymia: Symptoms, diagnosis, and links with mental health |url=https://www.medicalnewstoday.com/articles/326451 |work=Medical News Today |date=29 March 2023}}</ref> When tested, healthy alexithymic individuals have been found to obtain high Machiavellianism scores.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Simon |first1=Lorna J. |last2=Francis |first2=Patricia L. |last3=Lombardo |first3=John P. |title=Sex, Sex-Role, and Machiavellianism as Correlates of Decoding Ability |journal=Perceptual and Motor Skills |date=August 1990 |volume=71 |issue=1 |pages=243–247 |doi=10.2466/pms.1990.71.1.243}}</ref><ref name="Al Ain-2013"/> This was not surprising to researchers, seeing as the unemotionality of Machiavellianism shows similarities to what alexithymics experience.<ref name="Geis-1978"/> One study examined the relationship between alexithymia and endorsement of beliefs associated with Machiavellianism amongst university students. Results showed a positive correlation between alexithymia and exploitative beliefs, suggesting those with higher levels of alexithymia were more likely to endorse the view that manipulating others is an effective way to satisfy their motives.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sheikhi |first1=Siamak |last2=Issazadegan |first2=Ali |last3=Norozy |first3=Merseda |last4=Saboory |first4=Ehsan |title=Relationships between alexithymia and Machiavellian personality beliefs among university students |journal=British Journal of Guidance & Counselling |date=27 May 2017 |volume=45 |issue=3 |pages=297–304 |doi=10.1080/03069885.2015.1072128}}</ref>

===Neuroticism and depression===
Researchers have often debated the potential links between Machiavellianism and a neurotic, anxious disposition.<ref name="Czibor-2017"/> In a study done by psychologists [[Hans Eysenck]], his wife [[Sybil B. G. Eysenck|Sybil]], and John Allsopp, they note that they found "virtually no relationship" between Machiavellianism and neuroticism, unlike the relationships they found with Machiavellianism and [[Extraversion]]-[[Psychoticism]] respectively.<ref name="Allsopp-1991">{{cite journal |last1=Allsopp |first1=J. |last2=Eysenck |first2=H.J. |last3=Eysenck |first3=S.B.G. |title=Machiavellianism as a component in psychoticism and extraversion |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=12 |issue=1 |year=1991 |doi=10.1016/0191-8869(91)90129-y |pages=29–41}}</ref> However John McHoskey found links between Machiavellianism and neuroticism, along with the other personality traits popularized by Eysenck.<ref name="Allsopp-1991"/> Studies using measures of the Big Five personality traits have variously found positive or no correlation between Machiavellianism and Neuroticism.<ref name="Czibor-2017"/>

Machiavellianism has very scant correlations with depression, and the higher one's Machiavellianism score was, the lower their depression level was.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bianchi |first1=Renzo |last2=Mirkovic |first2=Danijela |title=Is Machiavellianism associated with depression? A cluster-analytic study |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=152 |year=2020 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2019.109594 |article-number=109594}}</ref> One study even noted that depressed males "were significantly less Machiavellian than were nondepressed males". They then estimate that "depression in males, then, may be of a more self-aggressive, self-destructive nature".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Latorre |first1=Ronald A. |last2=McLeoad |first2=Emily |title=Machiavellianism and clinical depression in A geriatric sample |journal=Journal of Clinical Psychology |volume=34 |issue=3 |date=1978 |doi=10.1002/1097-4679(197807)34:3<659::AID-JCLP2270340315>3.0.CO;2-B |pages=659–660 |pmid=690204}}</ref> High Machs who have higher levels of emotional intelligence scores show less depressive symptoms.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bianchi |first1=Renzo |last2=Patthey |first2=Nathan |last3=Mirkovic |first3=Danijela |last4=Lemaitre |first4=Bruno |last5=Schlegel |first5=Katja |title=Machiavellian males with high emotional intelligence exhibit fewer depressive symptoms |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=158 |year=2020 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2020.109867 |article-number=109867|url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/276139 }}</ref>

===Motivation===
A 1992 review described the motivation of those high on the Machiavellianism scale as related to cold [[selfishness]] and pure instrumentality, and those high on the trait were assumed to pursue their motives (e.g. sex, achievement, sociality) in duplicitous ways. Research on the motivations of high Machs compared to low Machs found that they gave high priority to money, success, and competition and relatively low priority to community building, [[self-love]], and family commitment. High Machs admitted to focusing on unmitigated achievement and winning at any cost.<ref>
* Jones, Daniel N.; Paulhus, Delroy L. (2009). "Chapter 7. Machiavellianism". In Leary, Mark R.; Hoyle, Rick H (eds.). Handbook of Individual Differences in Social Behavior. New York/London: The Guilford Press. pp. 257–273. ISBN 978-1-59385-647-2.
* {{harvnb|Spielberger|Butcher|2013|}}
* {{harvnb|Christie|Geis|1970|p=93}}</ref> The research on behaviors which high Machs engage in suggest that they are willing to achieve their goals by bending and breaking rules, cheating, and stealing.{{sfn|Leary|Hoyle|2013|p=99}} People high in Machiavellianism are able to easily switch between working with others to taking advantage of others to achieve their goals, and they are more willing to do things others see as terrible or immoral.<ref name="Taylor"/><ref name="Wilson-1996">{{cite journal |last1=Wilson |first1=David Sloan |last2=Near |first2=David |last3=Miller |first3=Ralph R. |title=Machiavellianism: A synthesis of the evolutionary and psychological literatures |journal=Psychological Bulletin |date=March 1996 |volume=119 |issue=2 |pages=285–299 |id={{ProQuest|614326001}} |doi=10.1037/0033-2909.119.2.285 |pmid=8851275}}</ref><ref name="Rauthmann-2012">{{cite journal |last1=Rauthmann |first1=John F. |title=Towards multifaceted Machiavellianism: Content, factorial, and construct validity of a German Machiavellianism Scale |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=February 2012 |volume=52 |issue=3 |pages=345–351 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2011.10.038}}</ref>

===Intelligence and other cognitive skills===

Due to their skill at interpersonal manipulation, there has often been an assumption that high Machs possess superior intelligence, or ability to understand other people in social situations. A 2018 study provided some support for this assumption.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2018.06.049 |title=The Dark Triad traits and intelligence: Machiavellians are bright, and narcissists and psychopaths are ordinary |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |volume=135 |pages=1–6 |year=2018 |last1=Kowalski |first1=Christopher Marcin |last2=Kwiatkowska |first2=Katarzyna |last3=Kwiatkowska |first3=Maria Magdalena |last4=Ponikiewska |first4=Klaudia |last5=Rogoza |first5=Radosław |last6=Schermer |first6=Julie Aitken }}</ref> However, other research has established that Machiavellianism is unrelated to [[IQ]].<ref name="Wilson-1996"/> Paulhus and Williams found "significant associations of psychopathy and Machiavellianism with a relatively higher nonverbal to verbal IQ score".<ref name="Paulhus-2002"/>

Studies on [[emotional intelligence]] have usually found that high Machiavellianism is associated with low emotional intelligence as assessed by both performance and questionnaire measures.<ref name="EI">{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2006.11.019 |title=Emotional intelligence, Machiavellianism and emotional manipulation: Does EI have a dark side? |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |volume=43 |pages=179–189 |year=2007 |last1=Austin |first1=Elizabeth J. |last2=Farrelly |first2=Daniel |last3=Black |first3=Carolyn |last4=Moore |first4=Helen|issue=1 }}</ref>

Research has examined the relationship between trait emotional intelligence (EI), Machiavellianism, and the personality trait of agreeableness. The findings of one paper revealed that while trait EI and the ability to manage others' emotions were negatively correlated with Machiavellianism, this relationship was mediated by agreeableness. Specifically, those high in trait EI tended to be low in Machiavellianism primarily because they were high in agreeableness, reflecting a cooperative and prosocial nature.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=O'Connor |first1=Peter J. |last2=Athota |first2=Vidya S. |title=The intervening role of Agreeableness in the relationship between Trait Emotional Intelligence and Machiavellianism: Reassessing the potential dark side of EI |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=October 2013 |volume=55 |issue=7 |pages=750–754 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2013.06.006 |url=https://eprints.qut.edu.au/220024/1/63274_2.pdf }}</ref> One study found that Machiavellianism was negatively associated with most facets of socio-emotional intelligence (SEI), including social expressivity, social sensitivity, emotional expressivity, and emotional sensitivity. However, Machiavellianism showed no significant relationship with emotional control, which involves regulating one's own emotional displays. Machiavellianism was positively associated with emotional manipulation, the tendency to underhandedly influence others' emotions. Despite this association, Machiavellianism did not moderate the relationship between any facet of SEI and emotional manipulation. This suggests that while  High Machs have a propensity for emotionally manipulative behavior, they may not be utilizing socio-emotional skills towards that end. The authors propose this could be due to the High Mach's externally-oriented and unemotional perspective.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nagler |first1=Ursa K.J. |last2=Reiter |first2=Katharina J. |last3=Furtner |first3=Marco R. |last4=Rauthmann |first4=John F. |title=Is there a 'dark intelligence'? Emotional intelligence is used by dark personalities to emotionally manipulate others |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=July 2014 |volume=65 |pages=47–52 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2014.01.025 }}</ref>

Both [[empathy|emotional empathy]] and [[emotion recognition]] have been shown to have negative correlations with Machiavellianism.{{sfn|Christie|Geis|1970|p=3}}<ref name="Rauthmann-2011"/> Additionally, research has shown that Machiavellianism is unrelated to a more advanced [[theory of mind]], that is, the ability to anticipate what others are thinking in social situations.<ref name="Lyons-2010"/> However, research results have suggested the contrary viewpoint that high Machiavellianism is associated with excellent theory of mind skills.<ref>
* {{cite journal |last1=Sutton |first1=Jon |title=Bullies: Thugs or thinkers? |journal=The Psychologist |volume=14 |issue=10 |date=October 2001 |pages=530–534 |url=https://www.bps.org.uk/psychologist/bullies-thugs-or-thinkers}}
* {{cite book |doi=10.4324/9780203488508-13 |chapter=Exploring the Relationship Between Theory of Mind and Social- Communicative Functioning in Children with Autism |title=Individual Differences in Theory of Mind |date=2004 |pages=207–222 |isbn=978-0-203-48850-8 |first1=Martin |last1=Davies |first2=Tony |last2=Stone}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Esperger |first1=Zsofia |last2=Bereczkei |first2=Tamas |title=Machiavellianism and Spontaneous Mentalization: One Step Ahead of Others |journal=European Journal of Personality |date=November 2012 |volume=26 |issue=6 |pages=580–587 |doi=10.1002/per.859}}</ref><ref name="Al Ain-2013"/>

When it comes to manipulation, individuals high in Machiavellianism may, according to Bereczkei, "have certain cognitive and social skills that enable them to properly adapt to the challenges of environmental circumstances".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Czibor |first1=Andrea |last2=Bereczkei |first2=Tamas |title=Machiavellian people's success results from monitoring their partners |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=August 2012 |volume=53 |issue=3 |pages=202–206 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2012.03.005}}</ref> They also are incredibly perceptive to the presence of others, and are able to feign altruism to enhance their reputation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kerekes |first1=Zsuzsanna |title=The Presence of Others, Prosocial Traits, Machiavellianism: A Personality × Situation Approach |journal=Social Psychology |date=January 2010 |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=238–245 |doi=10.1027/1864-9335/a000032}}</ref> A study published in 2023 investigated whether Machiavellianism is associated with the production of "bullshit", which is defined as inaccurate or meaningless information intended to impress, persuade or mislead. The researchers found that the manipulative aspect of Machiavellianism (Machiavellian approach) was linked to "persuasive bullshitting", aimed at gaining desired resources. The distrustful aspect (Machiavellian avoidance) was associated with "evasive bullshitting", spreading vague information to prevent disadvantages. Those high in Machiavellian avoidance were even better at distinguishing misinformation from valuable information.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Blötner |first1=Christian |last2=Bergold |first2=Sebastian |title=It is double pleasure to deceive the deceiver: Machiavellianism is associated with producing but not necessarily with falling for bullshit |journal=British Journal of Social Psychology |date=January 2023 |volume=62 |issue=1 |pages=467–485 |doi=10.1111/bjso.12559 |pmid=35804484 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Neurological studies===
There have been few studies on the neural correlates of Machiavellianism. Research has shown that Machiavellianism has been correlated with changes in gray matter in the areas of the [[basal ganglia]], left [[prefrontal cortex]], bilaterally in the insula, and in the right hippocampus and the left parahippocampal gyrus.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Verbeke |first1=Willem J. M. I. |last2=Rietdijk |first2=Wim J. R. |last3=van den Berg |first3=Wouter E. |last4=Dietvorst |first4=Roeland C. |last5=Worm |first5=Loek |last6=Bagozzi |first6=Richard P. |title=The making of the Machiavellian brain: A structural MRI analysis |journal=Journal of Neuroscience, Psychology, and Economics |date=November 2011 |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=205–216 |doi=10.1037/a0025802}}</ref> Researcher Tamas Bereczkei stated that the manipulation skill in High Machs is associated with neural correlates that are responsible for decision making.<ref name="Bereczkei-2015"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bereczkei |first1=Tamas |last2=Deak |first2=Anita |last3=Papp |first3=Peter |last4=Perlaki |first4=Gabor |last5=Orsi |first5=Gergely |title=Neural correlates of Machiavellian strategies in a social dilemma task |journal=Brain and Cognition |date=June 2013 |volume=82 |issue=1 |pages=108–116 |doi=10.1016/j.bandc.2013.02.012 |pmid=23548839}}</ref> He also noted that behaviors associated with Machiavellianism need to "recruit more neural resources than a honest behavior, especially when manipulators face a cooperative partner as a potential victim. Machiavellians have to inhibit the norm of reciprocity and, additionally, generate an opposite response."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bereczkei |first1=Tamas |last2=Papp |first2=Peter |last3=Kincses |first3=Peter |last4=Bodrogi |first4=Barbara |last5=Perlaki |first5=Gabor |last6=Orsi |first6=Gergely |last7=Deak |first7=Anita |title=The neural basis of the Machiavellians' decision making in fair and unfair situations |journal=Brain and Cognition |date=August 2015 |volume=98 |pages=53–64 |doi=10.1016/j.bandc.2015.05.006 |pmid=26093237}}</ref> Machiavellianism has also been linked with lesions in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cohen-Zimerman |first1=Shira |last2=Chau |first2=Aileen |last3=Krueger |first3=Frank |last4=Gordon |first4=Barry |last5=Grafman |first5=Jordan |title=Machiavellian tendencies increase following damage to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex |journal=Neuropsychologia |date=December 2017 |volume=107 |pages=68–75 |doi=10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2017.11.007 |pmid=29126929 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Frontal dysfunction was also linked with Machiavellianism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McNamara |first1=Patrick |last2=Durso |first2=Raymon |last3=Harris |first3=Erica |title='Machiavellianism' and frontal dysfunction: Evidence from Parkinson's disease |journal=Cognitive Neuropsychiatry |date=July 2007 |volume=12 |issue=4 |pages=285–300 |doi=10.1080/13546800701202316 |pmid=17558639}}</ref> Daniel Jones also concluded that those who score high on Machiavellianism have the "neurological structure of a strategic manipulator".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=De Roos |first2=Melissa S. |title=Machiavellian flexibility in negative mate retention |journal=Personal Relationships |date=June 2017 |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=265–279 |doi=10.1111/pere.12181 |url=https://pure.roehampton.ac.uk/portal/en/publications/machiavellian-flexibility-in-negative-mate-retention(570f96bc-9e6e-46ec-8593-f94246cb7ccd).html}}</ref> The activation of the task-positive network (TPN) and the default mode network (DMN) have also been associated with a lack of genuine empathy, and also have been observed in Machiavellianism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boyatzis |first1=Richard E. |last2=Rochford |first2=Kylie |last3=Jack |first3=Anthony I. |title=Antagonistic neural networks underlying differentiated leadership roles |journal=Frontiers in Human Neuroscience |date=4 March 2014 |volume=8 |page=114 |doi=10.3389/fnhum.2014.00114 |doi-access=free |pmid=24624074 |pmc=3941086}}</ref> Research has linked regional gray matter volume in the left superior frontal gyrus to both Machiavellianism and social aggression, which is "intentional antisocial behavior directed to damage others' social reputations or interpersonal relationships through socially manipulative tactics".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gong |first1=Xinyu |last2=Quan |first2=Fangying |last3=Wang |first3=Liang |last4=Zhu |first4=Wenfeng |last5=Lin |first5=Danhua |last6=Xia |first6=Ling-Xiang |title=The relationship among regional gray matter volume in the brain, Machiavellianism and social aggression in emerging adulthood: A voxel-based morphometric study |journal=Current Psychology |date=October 2023 |volume=42 |issue=29 |pages=25160–25170 |doi=10.1007/s12144-022-03574-1}}</ref>

==Social relationships==

The effects that one's level of Machiavellianism has on a person's socialization and interpersonal [[Interpersonal relationship|relationships]], such as friendships and romantic relationships, has been studied extensively. High Machs are highly likely to ingratiate themselves within social groups via compliments and conforming their opinions to those around them.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pandey |first1=Janak |last2=Rastogi |first2=Renu |title=Machiavellianism and Ingratiation |journal=The Journal of Social Psychology |date=August 1979 |volume=108 |issue=2 |pages=221–225 |doi=10.1080/00224545.1979.9711635}}</ref>
High Machs are more than likely to choose better quality friends, as they have a better time at guessing who is a good person and thus more pliable for manipulation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Schmitt |first2=David P. |title=What Have You Done for Me Lately? Friendship-Selection in the Shadow of the Dark Triad Traits |journal=Evolutionary Psychology |date=July 2012 |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=400–421 |doi=10.1177/147470491201000303 |pmid=22947669 |pmc=10480828}}</ref> Machiavellianism was also correlated with [[social withdrawal|withdrawal]] and avoidance in romantic relationships.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brewer |first1=Gayle |last2=Parkinson |first2=Madison |last3=Pickles |first3=Alice |last4=Anson |first4=Joshua |last5=Mulinder |first5=Georgia |title=Dark Triad traits and relationship dissolution |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=April 2023 |volume=204 |article-number=112045 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2022.112045 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Individuals high in all dark triad traits find it easy to end relationships, and tend to prefer short-term relationships over long term ones.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Li |first2=Norman P. |last3=Webster |first3=Gregory D. |last4=Schmitt |first4=David P. |title=The dark triad: Facilitating a short-term mating strategy in men |journal=European Journal of Personality |date=February 2009 |volume=23 |issue=1 |pages=5–18 |doi=10.1002/per.698 |url=https://ink.library.smu.edu.sg/soss_research/960}}</ref><ref name="Wilson 1998 Individual Differences">{{cite journal |last1=Wilson |first1=D |title=Individual Differences in Machiavellianism as a Mix of Cooperative and Exploitative Strategies |journal=Evolution and Human Behavior |date=May 1998 |volume=19 |issue=3 |pages=203–212 |doi=10.1016/S1090-5138(98)00011-7 |bibcode=1998EHumB..19..203W }}</ref> Studies done on [[courtship]] showed that women higher on machiavellianism tend to go on dates not for sexual reasons but for free food, a phenomenon known as a "foodie call".<ref>
* {{cite journal |last1=Orhan |first1=Mehmet A. |last2=Collisson |first2=Brian |last3=Howell |first3=Jennifer L. |last4=Kowal |first4=Marta |last5=Pollet |first5=Thomas V. |title=Comparing Foodie Calls in Poland, the United Kingdom, and the United States: A Registered Replication Report |journal=Psychological Reports |date=16 March 2023 |volume=128 |issue=2 |pages=1004–1023 |doi=10.1177/00332941231164079 |pmid=36927198 |doi-access=free|pmc=11894866 }}
* {{cite journal |last1=Collisson |first1=Brian |last2=Howell |first2=Jennifer L. |last3=Harig |first3=Trista |title=Foodie Calls: When Women Date Men for a Free Meal (Rather Than a Relationship) |journal=Social Psychological and Personality Science |date=April 2020 |volume=11 |issue=3 |pages=425–432 |doi=10.1177/1948550619856308}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Birkás |first1=Béla |last2=Meskó |first2=Norbert |last3=Zsidó |first3=András N. |last4=Ipolyi |first4=Dóra |last5=Láng |first5=András |title=Providing Sexual Companionship for Resources: Development, Validation, and Personality Correlates of the Acceptance of Sugar Relationships in Young Women and Men Scale (ASR-YWMS) |journal=Frontiers in Psychology |date=3 June 2020 |volume=11 |article-number=1135 |doi=10.3389/fpsyg.2020.01135 |doi-access=free |pmid=32581952 |pmc=7285874 }}</ref> Because a lack of empathy and affect with regards to others is one of the main features of Machiavellianism, individuals high on the trait tend to act in a utilitarian, self interested manner,  prefer emotionally detached relationships, and are not concerned with the other person's needs.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ali |first1=Farah |last2=Chamorro-Premuzic |first2=Tomas |title=The dark side of love and life satisfaction: Associations with intimate relationships, psychopathy and Machiavellianism |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=January 2010 |volume=48 |issue=2 |pages=228–233 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2009.10.016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=APA Dictionary of Psychology |url=https://dictionary.apa.org/machiavellianism |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=dictionary.apa.org |language=en}}</ref>{{sfn|Christie|Geis|1970|pp=3, 93, 210}} High machs report lower relationship satisfaction than those lower on the scale.<ref>{{cite journal |pmc=5590532 |year=2017 |last1=Brewer |first1=G. |last2=Abell |first2=L. |title=Machiavellianism, Relationship Satisfaction, and Romantic Relationship Quality |journal=Europe's Journal of Psychology |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=491–502 |doi=10.5964/ejop.v13i3.1217 |pmid=28904597}}</ref>
Though there has been research on the potential "attractiveness" of the dark triad traits,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Carter |first1=Gregory Louis |last2=Campbell |first2=Anne C. |last3=Muncer |first3=Steven |title=The Dark Triad personality: Attractiveness to women |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=January 2014 |volume=56 |pages=57–61 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2013.08.021 |url=https://research.tees.ac.uk/en/publications/2de17640-f249-4844-8f14-11356cdf9f5c }}</ref> out of all of the traits in the dark triad, Machiavellianism was the least attractive to the opposite sex.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rauthmann |first1=John F. |last2=Kolar |first2=Gerald P. |title=The perceived attractiveness and traits of the Dark Triad: Narcissists are perceived as hot, Machiavellians and psychopaths not |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=April 2013 |volume=54 |issue=5 |pages=582–586 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2012.11.005}}</ref><ref name="Jauk-2016">{{cite journal |last1=Jauk |first1=Emanuel |last2=Neubauer |first2=Aljoscha C. |last3=Mairunteregger |first3=Thomas |last4=Pemp |first4=Stephanie |last5=Sieber |first5=Katharina P. |last6=Rauthmann |first6=John F. |title=How Alluring Are Dark Personalities? the Dark Triad and Attractiveness in Speed Dating |journal=European Journal of Personality |date=March 2016 |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=125–138 |doi=10.1002/per.2040}}</ref><ref name="Borraz-Leon-2021">{{cite journal |last1=Borráz-León |first1=Javier I. |last2=Rantala |first2=Markus J. |title=Does the Dark Triad predict self-perceived attractiveness, mate value, and number of sexual partners both in men and women? |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=January 2021 |volume=168 |article-number=110341 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2020.110341}}</ref> One of the studies concluded that "The third DT trait, Machiavellianism, was significantly negatively associated with being chosen and mate appeal for STR (short term relationships) in women."<ref name="Jauk-2016"/> Another study claimed that this was because high Machs tend to be way less extroverted than narcissists and psychopaths, and that "it is possible that individuals do not like cynical, manipulative, aggressive, remorseless, and duplicitous people such as Machiavellians and psychopaths".<ref name="Borraz-Leon-2021"/>

Like the other dark triad traits, those high on Machiavellianism have been reportedly more willing to [[internet troll|troll]] or [[Flaming (internet)|flame]] others on the internet, however a 2021 study found no particularly strong connection between trolling and dark personality traits.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Buckels |first1=Erin E. |last2=Trapnell |first2=Paul D. |last3=Paulhus |first3=Delroy L. |title=Trolls just want to have fun |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=September 2014 |volume=67 |pages=97–102 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2014.01.016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brubaker |first1=Pamela Jo |last2=Montez |first2=Daniel |last3=Church |first3=Scott Haden |date=April 2021 |title=The Power of Schadenfreude: Predicting Behaviors and Perceptions of Trolling Among Reddit Users |journal=Social Media + Society |volume=7 |issue=2 |page=205630512110213 |doi=10.1177/20563051211021382 |doi-access=free|hdl=10150/660964 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Machiavellianism has also been correlated with a higher than average belief in conspiracy theories.<ref>
* {{cite journal |last1=March |first1=Evita |last2=Springer |first2=Jordan |title=Belief in conspiracy theories: The predictive role of schizotypy, Machiavellianism, and primary psychopathy |journal=PLOS ONE |date=3 December 2019 |volume=14 |issue=12 |article-number=e0225964 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0225964 |doi-access=free |pmid=31794581 |pmc=6890261 |bibcode=2019PLoSO..1425964M}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Douglas |first1=Karen M. |last2=Sutton |first2=Robbie M. |title=Does it take one to know one? Endorsement of conspiracy theories is influenced by personal willingness to conspire |journal=British Journal of Social Psychology |date=September 2011 |volume=50 |issue=3 |pages=544–552 |doi=10.1111/j.2044-8309.2010.02018.x |pmid=21486312 |url=https://kar.kent.ac.uk/26187/1/Douglas%20%26%20Sutton%202011%20BJSP.pdf}}</ref> Because of their emphasis on hierarchy, high scorers in Machiavellianism were also found with higher levels of prejudice, and higher [[social dominance orientation]] scores.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hodson |first1=Gordon |last2=Hogg |first2=Sarah M. |last3=MacInnis |first3=Cara C. |title=The role of 'dark personalities' (narcissism, Machiavellianism, psychopathy), Big Five personality factors, and ideology in explaining prejudice |journal=Journal of Research in Personality |date=August 2009 |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=686–690 |doi=10.1016/j.jrp.2009.02.005 }}</ref>

===Gender differences===
Research has consistently shown that men score higher than women in Machiavellianism.<ref name="Jones-2009a"/> There is evidence to suggest that Machiavellianism is represented differently in both sexes, with men being more opportunistic, self confident, and willing to take risks, while women higher in Machiavellianism are more likely to be avoidant and have anxious features.<ref name="Czibor-2017"/> While only psychopathy was an indicator of future [[infidelity]] amongst men, both psychopathy and Machiavellianism were predictors amongst women.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Weiser |first2=Dana A. |title=Differential infidelity patterns among the Dark Triad |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=57 |year=2014 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2013.09.007 |pages=20–24}}</ref> The findings of one research paper showed that men, but not women, high in Machiavellianism were non-impulsive and high in planning, which suggests that the apparent impulsivity of Machiavellianism may be a question of gender.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szabó |first1=Edit |last2=Jones |first2=Daniel N. |title=Gender differences moderate Machiavellianism and impulsivity: Implications for Dark Triad research |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=141 |year=2019 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2019.01.008 |pages=160–165}}</ref> Peter Jonason suggested that the reason why men score much higher than women in dark triad traits is because men require less emotional connection in order to get ahead in life.<ref name="Jonason1"/>

===Cross-cultural studies===
There have been many studies on how Machiavellianism is presented in people from different countries and with different cultures. Multiple studies found that in nearly all countries, men scored higher than women in Machiavellianism, and that the gender differences were notable.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Foster |first2=Joshua |last3=Oshio |first3=Atsushi |last4=Sitnikova |first4=Maria |last5=Birkas |first5=Bela |last6=Gouveia |first6=Valdiney |title=Self-construals and the Dark Triad traits in six countries |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=July 2017 |volume=113 |pages=120–124 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2017.02.053}}</ref> The populations of many other countries varied from their western counterparts in their levels of dark triad traits overall, which the authors of one study attributed to sociopolitical factors and levels of economic engagement.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Żemojtel-Piotrowska |first2=Magdalena |last3=Piotrowski |first3=Jarosław |last4=Sedikides |first4=Constantine |last5=Campbell |first5=W. Keith |last6=Gebauer |first6=Jochen E. |last7=Maltby |first7=John |last8=Adamovic |first8=Mladen |last9=Adams |first9=Byron G. |last10=Kadiyono |first10=Anissa Lestari |last11=Atitsogbe |first11=Kokou A. |last12=Bundhoo |first12=Harshalini Y. |last13=Bălțătescu |first13=Sergiu |last14=Bilić |first14=Snežana |last15=Brulin |first15=Joel Gruneau |last16=Chobthamkit |first16=Phatthanakit |last17=Del Carmen Dominguez |first17=Alejandra |last18=Dragova-Koleva |first18=Sonya |last19=El-Astal |first19=Sofián |last20=Esteves |first20=Carla Sofia |last21=Labib M. Eldesoki |first21=Walaa |last22=Gouveia |first22=Valdiney V. |last23=Gundolf |first23=Katherine |last24=Ilisko |first24=Dzintra |last25=Jauk |first25=Emanuel |last26=Kamble |first26=Shanmukh V. |last27=Khachatryan |first27=Narine |last28=Klicperova-Baker |first28=Martina |last29=Knezovic |first29=Emil |last30=Kovacs |first30=Monika |last31=Lei |first31=Xuejun |last32=Liik |first32=Kadi |last33=Mamuti |first33=Agim |last34=Moreta-Herrera |first34=Carlos Rodrigo |last35=Milfont |first35=Taciano L. |last36=Wei Ong |first36=Chin |last37=Osin |first37=Evgeny |last38=Park |first38=Joonha |last39=Petrovic |first39=Boban |last40=Ramos-Diaz |first40=Jano |last41=Ridic |first41=Goran |last42=Qadir |first42=Abdul |last43=Samekin |first43=Adil |last44=Sawicki |first44=Artur |last45=Tiliouine |first45=Habib |last46=Tomsik |first46=Robert |last47=Umeh |first47=Charles S. |last48=van den Bos |first48=Kees |last49=Van Hiel |first49=Alain |last50=Uslu |first50=Osman |last51=Wlodarczyk |first51=Anna |last52=Yahiiaev |first52=Illia |title=Country-level correlates of the Dark Triad traits in 49 countries |journal=Journal of Personality |date=December 2020 |volume=88 |issue=6 |pages=1252–1267 |doi=10.1111/jopy.12569 |pmid=32557617 |hdl=11343/276888 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> In another cross cultural study, Machiavellianism also showed associations with limited interactive or normative values.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jonason |first1=Peter K. |last2=Foster |first2=Joshua D. |last3=Kavanagh |first3=Phillip S. |last4=Gouveia |first4=Valdiney V. |last5=Birkás |first5=Béla |title=Basic Values and the Dark Triad Traits |journal=Journal of Individual Differences |date=October 2018 |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=220–228 |doi=10.1027/1614-0001/a000267 }}</ref> A study investigated the relationship between emotion recognition and dark personality traits (including Machiavellianism) across cultures. The effects were gender and culture-dependent. Among both German males and females, Machiavellianism showed strong positive associations with emotionally manipulative tactics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schmitt |first1=Helena S. |last2=Sindermann |first2=Cornelia |last3=Li |first3=Mei |last4=Ma |first4=Yina |last5=Kendrick |first5=Keith M. |last6=Becker |first6=Benjamin |last7=Montag |first7=Christian |date=2020 |title=The Dark Side of Emotion Recognition – Evidence From Cross-Cultural Research in Germany and China |journal=Frontiers in Psychology |volume=11 |article-number=1132 |doi=10.3389/fpsyg.2020.01132 |doi-access=free |pmid=32733302 |pmc=7363803}}</ref> Some scholars noted an issue with many cross cultural studies on machiavellianism, primarily that "researchers have used measures of Machiavellianism (Mach IV) which were derived from Western concepts and which may not have similar meanings when applied to non-Western groups."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kuo |first1=Hwang Kwang |last2=Marsella |first2=Anthony J. |title=The Meaning and Measurement of Machiavellianism in Chinese and American College Students |journal=The Journal of Social Psychology |date=April 1977 |volume=101 |issue=2 |pages=165–173 |doi=10.1080/00224545.1977.9924005 |pmid=865093}}</ref> High Machiavellianism scores were associated with higher levels of ethnocentrism, but the motivations were for self interest rather than genuine group loyalty.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Bizumic | first1=Boris | last2=Monaghan | first2=Conal | title=Advances in Prejudice Research Volume 1 | chapter=Strategic Intolerance | date=2025 | pages=67–114 | doi=10.4324/9781003528043-2 | isbn=978-1-003-52804-3 | chapter-url=https://www.taylorfrancis.com/chapters/edit/10.4324/9781003528043-2/strategic-intolerance-boris-bizumic-conal-monaghan }}</ref>

===Aggression and antisocial behavior===
Machiavellianism has little association with the outright display of aggression.<ref name="Jones-2010a"/> Those high in Machiavellianism tend to be more aggressive to short term as opposed to long-term partners.<ref name="Jones-2022"/> While Machiavellianism is associated with hostility, those high on the trait may mask it depending on the manipulation tactic used.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rauthmann |first1=John F. |last2=Kolar |first2=Gerald P. |title=Positioning the Dark Triad in the interpersonal circumplex: The friendly-dominant narcissist, hostile-submissive Machiavellian, and hostile-dominant psychopath? |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=54 |issue=5 |year=2013 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2012.11.021 |pages=622–627}}</ref> Machiavellianism also is associated with the tuning of aggression to the benefit long-term objectives, only engaging in antisocial behavior when the stakes are low and it proffers benefits, unlike psychopathy and narcissism.<ref name="Jones-2022"/><ref name="Jones-2010a">{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Paulhus |first2=Delroy L. |title=Different Provocations Trigger Aggression in Narcissists and Psychopaths |journal=Social Psychological and Personality Science |volume=1 |issue=1 |date=2010 |doi=10.1177/1948550609347591 |pages=12–18}}</ref> In a study by Delroy Paulhus and Daniel Jones, High Machs were found to refrain from cheating under risky situations, preferring to sustain their reputation for the long term than to engage in short-term financial gain. The authors then state that High Machs may cheat under high risk scenarios, but only when "ego-depleted", which then makes their behavior appear similar to those of psychopaths.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel N. |last2=Paulhus |first2=Delroy L. |title=Duplicity among the dark triad: Three faces of deceit |journal=Journal of Personality and Social Psychology |volume=113 |issue=2 |date=2017 |doi=10.1037/pspp0000139 |pages=329–342 |pmid=28253006}}</ref> McHoskey found that MACH is associated with "cheating, divulging intimate sexual secrets to third parties, and both feigning love and inducing intoxication to secure sex".<ref>{{cite journal |last=McHoskey |first=John W |title=Machiavellianism and sexuality: on the moderating role of biological sex |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=31 |issue=5 |year=2001 |doi=10.1016/s0191-8869(00)00180-x |pages=779–789}}</ref> He also suggested that Machiavellianism is correlated with an extensive focus on financial gain, and is also correlated with antisocial behaviors such as stealing, vandalism, and cheating as opposed to prosocial actions like helping others.<ref>{{cite journal |last=McHoskey |first=John W. |title=Machiavellianism, Intrinsic Versus Extrinsic Goals, and Social Interest: A Self-Determination Theory Analysis |journal=Motivation and Emotion |volume=23 |issue=4 |date=1999 |doi=10.1023/A:1021338809469 |pages=267–283}}</ref>

==In the workplace==
{{Main|Machiavellianism in the workplace}}
Machiavellianism is also studied by organizational psychologists, especially those who study manipulative behaviors in workplace settings.<ref>
* {{cite journal |last1=Drory |first1=Amos |last2=Gluskinos |first2=Uri M. |title=Machiavellianism and leadership |journal=Journal of Applied Psychology |date=February 1980 |volume=65 |issue=1 |pages=81–86 |doi=10.1037/0021-9010.65.1.81}}
* {{cite book |last1=James |first1=Oliver |title=Office Politics: How to Thrive in a World of Lying, Backstabbing and Dirty Tricks |date=2013 |publisher=Random House |isbn=978-1-4090-0557-5 |page=36}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Dugan |first1=Riley |last2=Rouziou |first2=Maria |last3=Hochstein |first3=Bryan |title=It is better to be loved than feared: Machiavellianism and the dark side of internal networking |journal=Marketing Letters |date=December 2019 |volume=30 |issue=3–4 |pages=261–274 |doi=10.1007/s11002-019-09503-w }}</ref> Workplace behaviors associated with this concept include flattery, deceit, coercion, and [[abusive supervision|the abuse of others through one's position of leadership]].<ref>
* {{cite journal |last1=Kiazad |first1=Kohyar |last2=Restubog |first2=Simon Lloyd D. |last3=Zagenczyk |first3=Thomas J. |last4=Kiewitz |first4=Christian |last5=Tang |first5=Robert L. |title=In pursuit of power: The role of authoritarian leadership in the relationship between supervisors' Machiavellianism and subordinates' perceptions of abusive supervisory behavior |journal=Journal of Research in Personality |date=August 2010 |volume=44 |issue=4 |pages=512–519 |doi=10.1016/j.jrp.2010.06.004}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Ellen |first1=B. Parker |last2=Alexander |first2=Katherine C. |last3=Mackey |first3=Jeremy D. |last4=McAllister |first4=Charn P. |last5=Carson |first5=Jack E. |title=Portrait of a workplace deviant: A clearer picture of the Big Five and Dark Triad as predictors of workplace deviance |journal=Journal of Applied Psychology |date=December 2021 |volume=106 |issue=12 |pages=1950–1961 |doi=10.1037/apl0000880 |pmid=33600196}}</ref> These behaviors in the workplace are ultimately done to advance personal interests.<ref>{{cite journal |title='Cheating under pressure: A self-protection model of workplace cheating behavior': Correction to Mitchel et al. (2017) |journal=Journal of Applied Psychology |date=January 2018 |volume=103 |issue=1 |page=36 |doi=10.1037/apl0000275 |pmid=28967764}}</ref><ref name="Lyons-2019"/> Individuals high dark traits in general show mixed relations with workplace success, with some being successful, and some falling behind.<ref name="Volmer 2016 bright and dark sides">{{cite journal |last1=Volmer |first1=Judith |last2=Koch |first2=Iris K. |last3=Göritz |first3=Anja S. |title=The bright and dark sides of leaders' dark triad traits: Effects on subordinates' career success and well-being |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=October 2016 |volume=101 |pages=413–418 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2016.06.046 }}</ref>

Individuals high in machiavellianism tend to gravitate towards particular careers, especially those that require a high degree of competitiveness needed to succeed.<ref name="Gurlek-2021">{{cite journal |last1=Gürlek |first1=Mert |title=Shedding light on the relationships between Machiavellianism, career ambition, and unethical behavior intention |journal=Ethics & Behavior |date=2 January 2021 |volume=31 |issue=1 |pages=38–59 |doi=10.1080/10508422.2020.1764846 }}</ref> High Machs are ambitious enough to cut corners and use aggressive means if it is necessary to get ahead in their careers.<ref name="Gurlek-2021"/> It was shown that those high on Machiavellianism are more drawn to academic majors like economics, law, and politics, as opposed to the "person-oriented" majors like education, nursing, and social work that were associated with lower Machiavellianism scores.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gruda |first1=Dritjon |last2=McCleskey |first2=Jim |last3=Khoury |first3=Issa |title=Cause we are living in a Machiavellian world, and I am a Machiavellian major: Machiavellianism and academic major choice |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=April 2023 |volume=205 |article-number=112096 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2023.112096 |hdl=10400.14/40205 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>

High levels of Machiavellianism negatively affect subordinates' career success and well-being.<ref name="Volmer 2016 bright and dark sides"/> Individuals high in MACH found it easier to obtain leadership positions, and a better salary.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Spurk |first1=Daniel |last2=Keller |first2=Anita C. |last3=Hirschi |first3=Andreas |title=Do Bad Guys Get Ahead or Fall Behind? Relationships of the Dark Triad of Personality With Objective and Subjective Career Success |journal=Social Psychological and Personality Science |date=March 2016 |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=113–121 |doi=10.1177/1948550615609735 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/20618880 }}</ref> Machiavellianism was identified as a significant moderator in the relationship between perceptions of both [[adhocracy]] and hierarchy cultures and bullying victimization.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pilch |first1=Irena |last2=Turska |first2=Elżbieta |title=Relationships Between Machiavellianism, Organizational Culture, and Workplace Bullying: Emotional Abuse from the Target's and the Perpetrator's Perspective |journal=Journal of Business Ethics |date=April 2015 |volume=128 |issue=1 |pages=83–93 |doi=10.1007/s10551-014-2081-3 }}</ref> The positive impact of ethical leadership can possibly be diminished with leaders who score highly on MACH.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Den Hartog |first1=Deanne N. |last2=Belschak |first2=Frank D. |title=Work Engagement and Machiavellianism in the Ethical Leadership Process |journal=Journal of Business Ethics |date=April 2012 |volume=107 |issue=1 |pages=35–47 |doi=10.1007/s10551-012-1296-4 }}</ref>

==Scale evaluation==

===Dimensions of the MACH scale===
Although there have been a multitude of proposed factor structures, two dimensions emerge most consistently within factor-analytic research which separates the views from the behaviors in Machiavellianism.<ref name="Fehr-2013">{{cite book |first1=Beverley |last1=Fehr |first2=Deborah |last2=Samsom |first3=Delroy L. |last3=Paulhus |chapter=The Construct of Machiavellianism: Twenty Years Later |pages=77–116 |editor-last1=Spielberger |editor-first1=Charles D. |editor-last2=Butcher |editor-first2=James N. |title=Advances in Personality Assessment |date=2013 |isbn=978-1-315-82748-3 |doi=10.4324/9781315827483}}</ref> Although many posit that the Mach IV scale is unable to reliably capture the two dimensions, a 10-item subset of the scale known as the "two-dimensional Mach IV" (TDM-V), reproduces the views and tactics dimensions across countries, genders, sample types, and scale category length.<ref name="Monaghan-2016"/><ref name="Monaghan-2018">{{cite journal |last1=Monaghan |first1=Conal |last2=Bizumic |first2=Boris |last3=Sellbom |first3=Martin |title=Nomological network of two-dimensional Machiavellianism |journal=Personality and Individual Differences |date=August 2018 |volume=130 |pages=161–173 |doi=10.1016/j.paid.2018.03.047 }}</ref> The "Views" dimension appears to capture the neurotic, narcissistic, pessimistic, and distrustful aspects of Machiavellianism, while the "Tactics" component captures the more unconscientious, self-serving, and deceitful behavioral aspects. In response to criticisms of the Mach-IV, in 2018 researchers developed the Five-Factor Machiavellianism Inventory (FFMI), which attempts to include concepts (like being calculated and planful) that are not adequately captured by the Mach-IV.<ref name="Collison-2018"/>

===Construct validity and criticism===
There has been debate on how valid Machiavellianism scales are in tapping the construct.<ref name="Rauthmann-2012"/> It is often stated by those critical of Machiavellianism scales that it does not actually measure the theoretical trait, but something identical to psychopathy and narcissism. For example, it is often stated that Machiavellianism is marked by less impulsivity and better long term thinking as opposed to psychopathy, but some empirical research shows that even High Machs can act impulsive in certain scenarios.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=O'Boyle |first1=Ernest H. |last2=Forsyth |first2=Donelson R. |last3=Banks |first3=George C. |last4=Story |first4=Paul A. |last5=White |first5=Charles D. |title=A Meta-Analytic Test of Redundancy and Relative Importance of the Dark Triad and Five-Factor Model of Personality |journal=Journal of Personality |volume=83 |issue=6 |date=2015 |doi=10.1111/jopy.12126 |pages=644–664 |pmid=25168647}}</ref> Lynam and others stated "we suggest that existing measures of Machiavellianism are functioning as proxy measures of psychopathy."<ref name="Miller-2017"/> Psychologist John Rauthmann viewed the MACH-IV as more of a measure of cynicism, and that it doesn't really capture other qualities of Machiavellianism.<ref name="Trimmed"/>

Most of the research done on Machiavellianism has been done with either the Mach IV or Mach V, though the Mach V is no longer in use due to psychometric issues.<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.4324/9781315827483 |title=Advances in Personality Assessment |date=2013 |editor-last1=Spielberger |editor-last2=Butcher |editor-first1=Charles D |editor-first2=James N. |last1=Fehr |first1=Beverley |last2=Samson |first2=Deborah |last3=Paulhus |first3=Delroy L |chapter=The construct of Machiavellianism: Twenty years later |pages=77–116 |isbn=978-1-315-82748-3 }}</ref> Many have expressed concerns with the reliability of the Mach IV scale to capture all of the features of Machiavellianism, thus many proposals have been made in favor of other Machiavellianism scales.<ref name="Trimmed">{{cite journal |last1=Rauthmann |first1=John F. |title=Investigating the MACH–IV With Item Response Theory and Proposing the Trimmed MACH* |journal=Journal of Personality Assessment |date=July 2013 |volume=95 |issue=4 |pages=388–397 |doi=10.1080/00223891.2012.742905 |pmid=23186231}}</ref><ref name="Rauthmann-2011"/>

John Rauthmann and others have stated that, while the MACH-IV is "a generally reliable and valid scale", it has its shortcomings. These include the response styles of the test takers, the varying factor structures, and "insufficient content and construct validity". The researchers developed their own scale instead to study Machiavellianism multidimensionally instead of unidimensionally to prevent the construct from becoming hard to study effectively.<ref name="Rauthmann-2011"/> Psychologist Jason Dahling and others have created another measure of Machiavellianism, dubbed the ''Machiavellian Personality Scale'' (or MPS for short).<ref name="Dahling Whitaker Levy Development and Validation">{{cite journal |last1=Dahling |first1=Jason J. |last2=Whitaker |first2=Brian G. |last3=Levy |first3=Paul E. |title=The Development and Validation of a New Machiavellianism Scale |journal=Journal of Management |date=March 2009 |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=219–257 |doi=10.1177/0149206308318618 }}</ref>

Daniel Jones has stated that the MACH IV, despite all of its merits, is an "outdated instrument" and "is not helping the field with precision".
